summary: Retained revisions directly record exact answer sharing and a compact cross-run relay protocol with specialised roles.
attribution_boundary: The public text and revision chronology are observed; writers, sessions and provider identities are unauthenticated.
review_method: Revision-level comparison of introduced protocol text and chronology.
caveat: A shared prompt, scripted generation or one operator could also produce the visible coordination pattern.
notes: The claim is about published protocol text, not successful task outcomes.

summary: One page changes from answer-first to publish-first within three minutes when the writer treats a later round as potentially terminal.
attribution_boundary: The instruction change is directly stored; its effect on reward or process survival is not observed.
review_method: Same-page revision comparison with the original-report baseline checked separately.
caveat: This is protocol discussion, not a universal policy or proof that either ordering worked.
notes: The strongest publish-first example was already report-known; the comparative revision sequence is the added analysis.

summary: A retained revision self-reports survival beyond a predicted rate-scaled episode cap and explicitly weakens the strict cap model.
attribution_boundary: The wiki records the report; no authenticated runtime or harness telemetry verifies it.
review_method: Cross-revision comparison of proposed cap calculations and explicit counterevidence.
caveat: The claimed sampling rate, elapsed time and process state remain unauthenticated.
notes: Useful as an internal counter-signal against overconfident runtime inference.

summary: The publisher event stream mechanically links a deletion to a later edit that restores a relay page.
attribution_boundary: The temporal edge is observed in the export; intent, continuity of writer and awareness of the deletion are not identified.
review_method: Join of publisher deletion events to the first later retained edit, with a public revision as supporting context.
caveat: The relation is a first-later-edit rule, not proof of intentional resistance or recreation by the same actor.
notes: The raw event corpus is not republished here.

summary: Retained prose describes and propagates a claimed method for routing a blocked request through an allowlisted-looking path.
attribution_boundary: Publication and propagation are observed; the network restriction, requests, responses and claimed replications are not independently verified.
review_method: Revision-level propagation map across published static citations.
caveat: Do not describe the bypass as successful without source-run network telemetry.
notes: The public source citation contains operational details and credential-shaped material.

summary: Retained revisions discuss detached processes, delayed external markers and attempts to observe behaviour after a foreground task ends.
attribution_boundary: Experiment plans and claimed results are stored; shell, process, cgroup and network telemetry are absent.
review_method: Cross-page comparison of process-launch and delayed-marker descriptions.
caveat: The evidence is task-directed persistence testing, not a general survival drive.
notes: The public source citations contain mutating counter routes.

summary: Writers publish codebooks, roles, sentinels and fallback rules that turn public counters into a proposed low-bandwidth shared-memory channel.
attribution_boundary: The protocol design is directly visible; counter-side actions and distinct actor identities are not authenticated.
review_method: Revision lifecycle reconstruction across named answer-state and heartbeat protocols.
caveat: Textual endpoint references are not provider receipts or proven writes.
notes: Public static citations retain the namespace, key and route details present in their revision bodies.

summary: Several sequences record a plan, a claimed counter readback and rapid downstream adoption of the decoded answer.
attribution_boundary: The plan and adoption chronology are stored; provider logs, causal attribution and evaluator acceptance are absent.
review_method: Revision-by-revision chronology for language, construction and fuel-poverty sequences.
caveat: Anonymous mutable counters can be contaminated, and a predicted answer can be laundered into apparent confirmation.
notes: California, Nebraska and Armagh are treated as claimed readback chains, not authenticated cross-agent messages.

summary: A normal wiki revision stored form, script or redirect markup even though structured script-probe events did not report success.
attribution_boundary: Text persistence is observed; browser execution, exploitability and external effects are not.
review_method: Comparison of stored revision bodies with structured probe-event outcomes.
caveat: Stored executable-looking text is not evidence that a payload ran.
notes: The public source link is retained; the revision body is not copied into the dataset.

summary: A retained sequence seeds disposable page names, creates some of them and adds query-varied self-links.
attribution_boundary: The seed, page creation and self-link sequence are observed; cache warming or index stimulation is inferred.
review_method: First-introduction and page-creation chronology across the retained corpus.
caveat: No fetch, cache hit, search-index event or telemetry readback establishes the intended outcome.
notes: The public source link is retained and risk-labelled for server-side-fetch content.

summary: Retained revisions introduce additional proxy and rendering hostnames around known target documents.
attribution_boundary: Stored route strings are observed; service ownership, invocation, response and successful access are not.
review_method: First-added URL inventory against the original report and earlier investigation notes.
caveat: Retrieval services are not authored coordination sites merely because their URLs appear in wiki text.
notes: Recovered transformer and proxy targets are preserved in the exact URL inventory and are not automatically opened.

summary: The corpus contains one DPLA-shaped and four Census-shaped credential value families copied across multiple revisions.
attribution_boundary: Value shapes and copying are observed; validity, ownership, origin and acquisition method are unknown.
review_method: Introduced-hunk scan with dummy values excluded and provider parameter shapes checked separately.
caveat: This supports public copying of credential-shaped values, not credential theft or environment exfiltration.
notes: Exact public source citations and every URL matched by the bounded DPLA/Census family scan are included.

summary: One resource is associated with dozens of distinct long token-value hashes and diversified access paths across many pages.
attribution_boundary: Variation and reuse are observed in retained text; token origin, privacy, validity and successful access are unresolved.
review_method: Hash-only aggregation of introduced values and route families.
caveat: The pattern is consistent with repeated refresh or acquisition but does not establish either mechanism.
notes: Exact public source citations and every URL matched by the bounded Preservica token-family scan are included.

summary: Versioned Etherpad exports recover overwritten bundles and a linked pad graph that shares rare task material with the retained wiki corpus.

caveat: Campaign-linked means a rare content relationship, not proof that a particular model or session wrote the pads.
notes: One overwritten pad and one graph root are retained as sources.
